canonical_user_question: Should I set the fader balance before adding EQ and compression?
clarification_questions: Can you identify the lead element and the section where the arrangement is fullest?
Does the balance change drastically when you listen quietly?
common_mistakes: Using meter numbers as artistic targets.
Changing multiple faders and processors at once.
copyright_handling: Original paraphrased synthesis; no raw forum body or long quotation included.
do_not_assume: A meter, spectrum, fader position, or common forum setting determines the artistic answer.
The most popular suggestion is correct for this source and arrangement.
A louder result is automatically better.
logic_pro_steps: Save a project alternative or note the current fader values.
Bypass nonessential mix processing without changing routing.
Set a representative loop and lower all musical faders.
Bring up the anchor element, then add one role at a time.
Restore processing and level-match the comparison.
logic_version_scope: Logic Pro 12.x; reverify visible labels and current project behavior on the installed version
natural_language_variants: Do I balance all the tracks before using plugins?
Should I get a rough mix with only faders first?
Am I supposed to EQ before I even set the levels?
rationale: This question concerns the difference between technical signal level, perceived loudness, and musical hierarchy. The useful answer depends on where the level changes and what role the source serves.

recommended_first_experiment.action: Bypass nonessential processing, loop the fullest representative section, and build a 60-second fader-only hierarchy from the most important element outward.
recommended_first_experiment.summary: Bypass nonessential processing, loop the fullest representative section, and build a 60-second fader-only hierarchy from the most important element outward.
recommended_first_experiment.why_this_first: It is intended to distinguish likely causes before adding more processing or making a permanent move.

starting_points: Choose one musical anchor rather than starting every fader at the same apparent meter value.
Work at a consistent, comfortable monitoring level.
stop_rule: Stop when the hierarchy reads clearly and further moves become smaller than the musical uncertainty.
teaching_principle: Balance is a relationship among musical roles, not a collection of target meter numbers.
title: Building a static balance before processing
tradeoffs_and_risks: A fader-only pass cannot solve severe tone or dynamics problems.
A single loop may not represent every section.
undo_or_reset: Restore the saved fader, gain, routing, automation, and plug-in state before testing another explanation.
what_to_listen_for: The song’s focal point should remain obvious at low playback level.
Supporting parts should be audible without competing equally.
